solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loss of all hope as pride is shattered

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into bits that can be put back together in another order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone's pride is broken and they lose all hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' reads like a joining word in the surface but supplies two of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the state of having given up all hope, a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Talk of wrongdoing carrying over after athletic event

indicators.note: the wrongdoing part is placed after the athletic event part

parts.note: throwing the discus is a field event in athletics

indicators.note: a word carrying something holds it inside itself

parts.note: a sin is a wrong act
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Gossip about some cheating after a track and field contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a cricket term here: the six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A discussion is a conversation on a topic, so talk as a noun fits.

clue.text: Street with station

parts.note: standard abbreviation for street
'and' means together with

explanation.surface: An address: a street that has a railway station on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand is a place where someone is posted or a vehicle waits, as in a taxi stand, so a station.

clue.text: Like standard uninspiring sweetener

parts.note: 'as' means like, in a comparison
par is the standard or normal level
tame means dull and unexciting

explanation.surface: A complaint that an ordinary artificial sweetener is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial sugar substitute used in diet drinks, an example of a sweetener.

clue.text: Regularly missing orders, Renault shut once more

indicators.note: dropping letters at regular intervals leaves every other one standing

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and so on letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Requests for a Renault car factory to close again.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd letters o, d, r, r, n, u, t go; the even ones remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To reseal is to close up again, so the verb shut with once more.

clue.text: One attractive meal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal word for a good-looking person
second meaning: a course or plate of food

explanation.surface: A single appealing dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for a sexy person and also the everyday word for a prepared item of food.

clue.text: Couple you welcomed to party

indicators.note: a guest welcomed to a gathering is taken inside it

parts.note: a do is an informal party
text-speak spelling of you

explanation.surface: A host greets a couple of guests arriving at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair of people, typically performers, so a couple.

clue.text: Clever clogs merits a rum

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters come out oddly arranged

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a show-off deserves a glass of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective meaning peculiar. A clever clogs is a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartie is a self-satisfied know-all, the same idea as a smart alec or clever clogs.

clue.text: Almost completed bridge in Cheltenham, perhaps

indicators.note: something almost completed is short of its finish, so its final letter is missing

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the stretch between its supports

explanation.surface: A bridge in Cheltenham that is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is an English town famous for its mineral springs; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with mineral springs, and Cheltenham is a well-known English example.

clue.text: Tense test of cleric

parts.note: the past is a grammatical tense
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A nervous exam for a would-be clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for nerves but is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral means relating to a minister's care of his flock, so belonging to a cleric's work.

clue.text: Reportedly smash flimsy car part

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is chosen for how it is spoken

parts.note: to break is to smash, and it is said the same as the stopping device
light means slight or insubstantial

explanation.surface: A news story that a weak car component got smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake light is the red lamp at a car's rear that comes on when braking, a component of the vehicle.

clue.text: Subordinate to a Parisian, the German

parts.note: un is French for a
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and a German ranked below someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under someone means being lower in rank than them, so subordinate to.

clue.text: Judge particular bit erroneously, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A judge got one particular detail somewhat wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person who settles disputes, a synonym for judge.

clue.text: One taking small parts from tip, barely damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of their proper order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone salvaging small components from a rubbish dump that is only slightly damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' is British for a rubbish dump, and 'parts' suggests components until read as acting roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit player is an actor with only minor roles, so someone who takes small parts on stage or screen.

clue.text: End of credits before commercial broadcast

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of the word
pre is the prefix meaning before
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: TV scheduling: closing credits then an advert are shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a placement instruction but supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread news is to broadcast it, scattering it widely as a verb.

clue.text: Soldiers with others housed in rubbish hideout

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: something housed in another thing sits inside it

parts.note: tat is cheap junk
more soldiers, again the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Troops and their comrades are holed up in a squalid hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers serve twice: once for 'Soldiers' and again for the 'others', who are more of the same corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a quiet secluded place to withdraw to, a refuge or hideaway.

clue.text: Irregular line runs within sirloin, say

indicators.note: within means placed on the inside of the next word

parts.note: sirloin is one kind of steak
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A wavy line of fat running through a sirloin.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a long thin uneven mark or band, so an irregular line.

clue.text: Fighting using blades

definitions.meaning: first meaning: quarrelling, from British 'row' rhyming with cow
second meaning: propelling a boat with oars, whose flat ends are blades

explanation.walkthrough: 'blades' suggests knives in a fight, but they are oar blades.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a row is a noisy argument, and rowing is also pulling oars through water.

clue.text: Charged with hotel, one got stupidly busy

indicators.note: something charged with a thing is loaded or filled with it
done stupidly means done in a muddled way, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: the letters as written
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone charged a hotel bill and foolishly kept themselves busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like being billed, but it means loaded: the scrambled letters take H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go is an idiom for being constantly active, so busy.

clue.text: Behold mostly peaceful neighbourhood

definitions.note: used attributively, as in a neighbourhood shop

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
calm means peaceful

explanation.surface: Look at this largely tranquil residential area.
explanation.definitionFit: Local describes something belonging to the nearby area, as neighbourhood does used before a noun.

clue.text: Key personnel raced around

indicators.note: around suggests letters spun into different positions

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Important staff hurried about.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small core group of trained people at the heart of an organisation.

clue.text: Happiness priest found in fine metropolis

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a metropolis is a large city
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A clergyman finds contentment in a fine big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is a formal word for intense happiness or bliss.

clue.text: Some of family circle turned unfriendly

indicators.note: turned round means read in the opposite direction
some of means only a portion of the next words is taken

parts.note: letters running across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Part of the family became hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy manner is cold and hostile, a figurative sense meaning unfriendly.

clue.text: Follow idol around

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so read backwards

parts.note: an idol is a god worshipped as an image

explanation.surface: A fan trails their hero everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, as a verb.

clue.text: Leader of Thailand involved in state visit

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

parts.note: to say is to state

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the country

explanation.surface: The Thai head of government takes part in a state visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like part of 'state visit', but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a period spent somewhere as a guest, so a visit as a noun.

clue.text: Item of clothing fellow wrapped around limb

indicators.note: something wrapped around another encloses it

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A man has a piece of clothing wound around his arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is any single article of clothing.
